doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Leon Thomas, the creative 70s and technology
summary: Leon Thomas's yodeling brought the group together; Smith says the 70s were uniquely creative and early keyboards were easier.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Did Leon Thomas have that kind of flexibility?

Yeah, oh yeah. That was the thing about Leon, that’s how we all got together. Because I said well dang, how can you play more than one note? You know with a horn player, can’t play but one note at a time. But he has figured out ways to sound like he’s playing more than one note. Then Leon was doing yodeling. And then I was doing a little bit different things on the keyboard so Pharoah said man, you know why don’t we all just get together? And it worked. Because no one else was doing the yodeling at that time like Leon Thomas. And so that’s what I’m saying, for some reason back in the 70s everybody was creative. I think everybody, the people are saying now, because I did a concert in California in February. And they’re really into the 70s, I noticed the young kids are now. If you notice their dress, hairstyle, they are saying that the 70s was the most — musically and everything — was the most creative period that they can remember.

I wonder if that has anything to do with technology. If we look back on the 70s we sort of smile at the level of technology was so far behind where it is now, but as you say, there was some great creativity going on at that time.

Oh yeah. Because I mean, that’s a good point. Because the keyboards today they mess with me, because they’re far advanced. But the Fender Rhodes we just played, it was easy. And so Miles hooked up those pedals so let me hook those same pedals up to everything. For some reason it was easier. But now, oh man you try to go inside the keyboard and try to figure out what to do, you have to get a tech.
